title: Reading Between the Lines
text:
Poetry often uses rhythm and rhyme to make language memorable. A poet chooses each word carefully, because a single word can change the mood of an entire line. Many readers find that a poem becomes clearer after a second reading.

Some poems tell a story, while others focus on a single feeling or image. For example, a short poem about the sea might describe waves without ever mentioning sadness, yet the reader still senses loneliness. This is why interpretation plays such an important role in reading poetry.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does poetry often use to make language memorable?
What does the second paragraph say some poems focus on?
options: A story or a single feeling or image

questions.text: Why might a reader understand a poem better after reading it a second time?
options: The reader may notice details missed the first time

questions.text: What can be inferred about a short poem that describes waves without mentioning sadness?
options: The poet is describing a storm
The poem may still convey emotion through images
The poem is a scientific report

vocabulary.definition: the way a reader understands or explains the meaning of something

paragraph_translations: A poesia costuma usar ritmo e rima para tornar a linguagem memorável. Um poeta escolhe cada palavra cuidadosamente, porque uma única palavra pode mudar o clima de um verso inteiro. Muitos leitores percebem que um poema fica mais claro após a segunda leitura.

Alguns poemas contam uma história, enquanto outros se concentram em um único sentimento ou imagem. Por exemplo, um poema curto sobre o mar pode descrever ondas sem mencionar tristeza, mas o leitor ainda sente solidão. É por isso que a interpretação desempenha um papel tão importante na leitura de poesia.
